test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 09 Feb, 2026 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What will be the average of all the odd natural numbers between 6 and 44 ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In any Arithmetic Progression (AP), Average = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2.

The first odd number after 6 is 7.

The last odd number before 44 is 43.

Average = (7 + 43) ÷ 2 = 50 ÷ 2 = 25.

**∴ The correct answer is 25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Range of numbers from 6 to 44.

**Series:** Odd numbers between 6 and 44 are 7, 9, 11, ..., 43.

**Formula Used:** Average of an Arithmetic Progression = (a + l) ÷ 2, where a = first term and l = last term.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fa0a93e6f0354e34d8df7cd332a5c5cb20b796b3b6bd8fbbee52d69ea1c453c4.png] 

⇒ First odd number (a) = 7

⇒ Last odd number (l) = 43

⇒ This is an Arithmetic Progression with common difference d = 2.

⇒ Average = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2

⇒ Average = (7 + 43) ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 50 ÷ 2 = 25.

**∴ The correct answer is 25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Odd Numbers

The sum of the first n odd natural numbers is given by n².

Average of First n Odd Numbers

The average of the first n odd natural numbers is always equal to n.

Average of First n Natural Numbers

The average of the first n natural numbers is calculated as (n + 1) ÷ 2.

General AP Property

For any sequence in Arithmetic Progression, the average is always the middle term (if n is odd) or the mean of the two middle terms (if n is even).
